referents.why: 'You refusing' is second person in the LORD's words to Moses, which are addressed to Pharaoh (masculine singular).
'I' in the LORD's words (cl3 of the previous verse) is the LORD, the same person as the quoted speaker.
referents.category: first person of quoted divine speech

referents.why: 'your territory' is the possessive of the addressee, Pharaoh.

links.why: 'Refuse to let them go': the infinitive completes the verb of refusing as its object, and the purpose type excludes verbs of refusing.
The infinitive is nested as the object of 'refuse'.
The if-link runs from the host clause to its condition, so this direction is reversed.
The condition is 'if you refuse' (cl0); its host is the next clause that is not an infinitive complement, here (cl2).
This waw is the 'and' of 'and if' and is carried by the if-link; a second link duplicates it.
'Here, I am about to strike': a plain waw joining the consequence, with no cause or purpose.

groups.why: The if-clause and the clause it conditions; the consequence is cl2, the host of the apodosis.

none_fit.what: The exclamation that opens the consequence after a condition has no link type or group role; it is recorded as the host of the conditional's consequence.
